Notes: Dhakal p. 48 prints /bʰəike/ “to become” beside a separately negated form. Turner9416 gives Pali bhavati, Prakrit bhavaï, Ḍoḍi bhōṇō and other regional verbs “become”; Darai -ike is the regular infinitive, and its bhəi- stem matches the Middle Indo-Aryan bhavai family. Dhakal p. 54 prints /dziuno/ “living.” Turner5244 is the living participial family, with Kumaoni jyūno, Nepali jiũdo and Kotgarhi j̈iundɔ “living, alive.” These adjective comparanda select 5244 rather than noun jīva “life” (5239) or verbal jīvati (5241). Darai become, living, man, root and today; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild

Dhakal p. 54 gives /manus/ “man.” Turner9827 lists Prakrit manusa “man” and the inherited regional mánuṣa family; the Darai final s with final-vowel loss matches this branch better than the separate short mánus head 9825, whose cited NIA forms are manua/manū. Darai become, living, man, root and today; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild

Dhakal p. 56 prints /dzəri/ “root.” Turner5086 section 1 lists Nepali jari, Bihari jar, Maithili jaṛi and Oriya jaṛa with the same meaning. This identifies the regional root family, while Turner leaves its remoter Dravidian versus Munda history unsettled.
